segments.text: In this town, your shadow lives one day ahead of you.
Whatever it does today, you'll do tomorrow. So nobody here steals. If your shadow grabs a wallet tonight, the police are waiting for you in the morning.
Mayor Hale loves that. He put a streetlight on every corner. A town in the light, he says, is a town without secrets.
He always stands right under a lamp. He always wears his big hat. And he never comes outside at sunset.
Then, at the summer festival, it happened. Every shadow in the square turned around, and ran toward the town gate. Hundreds of them. But not one person moved.
Tomorrow, the whole town was going to run. Nobody knew why.
Mayor Hale stayed calm. More light, he said. He built a giant floodlight on the clock tower. Bright enough that nobody will ever see tomorrow coming.
Tonight, he asked me to help him switch it on. The sun was going down behind him, and for the first time in my life, I saw his shadow.
It was already standing outside the gate. Holding a suitcase full of the town's money. Waving goodbye.
The shadows weren't running from something. They were running after him.
Then I looked for my own shadow. It wasn't running after him. It was standing right next to his, holding the other handle of the suitcase.
Would you tell the town, or go with him?
